topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer and frames the lecture's aims within the cancer lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations give rise to cancer through clonal evolution shaped by cellular circumstances and inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence about environmental exposures challenges the view that cancer is simply unavoidable bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage through mechanisms that depend on their chemical properties and biological processing.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutagenic initiation may require a growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Developmental susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of carcinogenic mechanisms by explaining context-dependent susceptibility and recapping the mechanisms already discussed.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogenic exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how researchers identify carcinogenic exposures and evaluate carcinogenic potential despite limitations in the available evidence.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as judgments about risks and benefits.
